title: Nvidia in talks to backstop $250bn of OpenAI’s data-centre financing
excerpt: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to guarantee about $250bn of financing for OpenAI, a backstop that would let the ChatGPT maker fund a vast new data centre without the investment-grade credit rating such borrowing normally demands. content_html:
Nvidia is reportedly in talks to guarantee about $250bn of financing for OpenAI, a backstop that would let the ChatGPT maker fund a vast new data centre without the investment-grade credit rating such borrowing normally demands. The arrangement was described by the Wall Street Journal on July 26, and neither company has confirmed it.

The guarantee would not involve Nvidia handing over cash. It is a promise to cover the obligations if OpenAI or the project falls short, the sort of vendor support that has already drawn scrutiny as circular financing spreads through the AI economy. For a chipmaker that has spent the year making AI equity bets at a pace few rivals can match, it is another way of underwriting demand for its own hardware.

The money is tied to a 10-gigawatt campus in southern Ohio, developed by an energy subsidiary of SoftBank and leased by OpenAI, according to the Journal.

The $250bn would cover the data-centre lease and the construction debt behind it, with a further sum of up to $350bn discussed separately to fund chip purchases, potentially pushing the total project cost beyond $500bn.

The two tranches are being negotiated on different tracks, and none of the terms, including the fee Nvidia would charge for the guarantee, has been made public.

OpenAI does not carry an investment-grade rating, which makes borrowing on that scale expensive and, in places, impossible. Nvidia’s promise to stand behind the debt is what would make lenders comfortable, and it fits a wider shift in which OpenAI is trying to own more of its infrastructure rather than rent it from Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle.

Nvidia, for its part, secures years of guaranteed demand for the chips at the centre of the build, which is the whole point of standing behind someone else’s debt.

The talks extend a relationship the two firms formalised last autumn. In September 2025 Nvidia said it would invest up to $100bn in OpenAI as part of a partnership to deploy 10 gigawatts of its systems, a deal both sides billed at the time as the largest AI infrastructure project yet attempted.

If the guarantee now under discussion goes ahead, it would dwarf that commitment, turning a headline equity stake into a far larger and more entangled bet on OpenAI’s ability to pay.

The reception this weekend was sceptical. Michael Burry, the investor of The Big Short fame, wrote “around and around we go”, noting that Nvidia would be guaranteeing spending that ultimately flows back to Nvidia.

His post put the figure at $200bn, below the $250bn in the Journal’s account. The tech critic Ed Zitron called the structure “such an insane thing to do on so many levels”.

The unease is partly structural. A guarantee of this size behaves like a debt obligation on Nvidia’s balance sheet even if OpenAI never misses a payment, which could weigh on the company’s financial flexibility and invite questions from credit markets.

Nvidia has spent much of the cycle offering AI firms compute now, payment later, and a backstop of this kind is the same logic scaled up.

Capital may not even be the binding constraint. Power for the Ohio site is government-controlled, with allocation overseen by the US Commerce Secretary, Howard Lutnick, and part of the supply funded by Japan under a trade agreement, so the first phase is expected to bring only around 800 megawatts online in 2028.

OpenAI’s spending commitments now stretch well beyond what its revenue supports, from the Ohio hub to a separate $30bn data centre in Georgia. Nvidia shares closed on Friday down 0.92% at $206.84 and slipped further after hours.

We could not independently verify the report, no agreement has been signed, and neither company would comment, which leaves the largest number in the AI buildout so far resting on a single weekend report.

content_html_zh:
据报道，Nvidia 正在谈判为 OpenAI 提供约 2500 亿美元的融资担保，这一支持将使 ChatGPT 制造商能够为一个巨大的新数据中心提供资金，而无需此类借款通常要求的投资级信用评级。 《华尔街日报》7 月 26 日描述了这一安排，但两家公司均未予以证实。

该担保不涉及英伟达交出现金。 这是一种承诺，如果 OpenAI 或项目达不到要求，就会承担义务，随着循环融资在人工智能经济中蔓延，这种供应商支持已经受到了密切关注。 对于一家花了一年时间以很少有竞争对手能够匹敌的速度进行人工智能股票押注的芯片制造商来说，这是满足其自身硬件需求的另一种方式。

据《华尔街日报》报道，这笔资金与俄亥俄州南部一个 10 吉瓦的园区相关，该园区由软银的一家能源子公司开发，并由 OpenAI 租赁。

2500 亿美元将用于支付数据中心租赁及其背后的建设债务，另外高达 3500 亿美元的资金将单独讨论用于资助芯片采购，这可能会使项目总成本超过 5000 亿美元。

这两笔款项正在不同的轨道上进行谈判，所有条款（包括英伟达为担保收取的费用）都尚未公开。

OpenAI 没有投资级评级，这使得这种规模的借贷成本高昂，而且在某些地方是不可能的。 英伟达承诺为债务提供支持，这会让贷款人感到放心，而且它符合更广泛的转变，即 OpenAI 试图拥有更多的基础设施，而不是从微软、亚马逊和甲骨文那里租用。

就英伟达而言，它确保了对处于构建核心的芯片的多年需求保证，这就是支持别人债务的全部意义所在。

此次会谈延续了两家公司去年秋天正式建立的合作关系。 2025 年 9 月，英伟达表示将向 OpenAI 投资高达 1000 亿美元，作为合作伙伴关系的一部分，部署 10 吉瓦的系统，双方当时都宣称该交易是迄今为止最大的人工智能基础设施项目。

如果现在正在讨论的担保继续下去，那么这一承诺就会相形见绌，将主要股权变成对 OpenAI 支付能力的更大、更复杂的赌注。

这个周末的接待是持怀疑态度的。 因《大空头》而闻名的投资者迈克尔·伯里 (Michael Burry) 写道，“我们一直在走来走去”，指出英伟达将保证支出最终流回英伟达。

他的帖子称这一数字为 2000 亿美元，低于《华尔街日报》账上的 2500 亿美元。 技术评论家 Ed Zitron 称该结构“在如此多的层面上做起来都是一件疯狂的事情”。

这种不安部分是结构性的。 即使 OpenAI 从未错过付款，这种规模的担保在 Nvidia 的资产负债表上就像是债务义务，这可能会影响该公司的财务灵活性并引发信贷市场的问题。

英伟达在这个周期的大部分时间里都在为人工智能公司提供先计算、后付款的服务，这种支持的逻辑与扩大规模是一样的。

资本甚至可能不是约束性的约束。 俄亥俄州发电站的电力由政府控制，分配由美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 监督，部分供应由日本根据贸易协定提供资金，因此预计第一阶段到 2028 年将仅提供约 800 兆瓦的发电量。

OpenAI 的支出承诺现在远远超出了其收入支持的范围，从俄亥俄州中心到佐治亚州一个价值 300 亿美元的独立数据中心。 英伟达股价周五收盘下跌 0.92%，至 206.84 美元，盘后进一步下滑。

我们无法独立核实该报告，尚未签署任何协议，两家公司都不会发表评论，这使得迄今为止人工智能建设中最大的数字取决于单个周末报告。
